candidates.attacker_control: Any remote attacker holding valid credentials for a low-privileged account (authentication is the only gate on this URI; in Enterprise a "reader"/"editor" user suffices, in Community any account). The attacker fully controls the JSON body: engine ("SHELL") and the command string, e.g. a shell/Cypher command such as `call dbms.security.changeUserPassword('neo4j','attacker');` or `match (n) detach delete n;`. No other user-controlled state is required.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: Checked and excluded: (1) the URI is not in the authorization whitelist (AbstractNeo4jServer DEFAULT_URI_WHITELIST = "/", "/browser.*"), so unauthenticated requests are rejected 401 — confirmed by AuthorizationWhitelistIT line 68 and ManageNodeIT's default-enabled console test; the gap is authorization, not authentication. (2) No admin/role check exists in ConsoleService, ShellSession, ShellSessionCreator, ConsoleModule, AuthorizationEnabledFilter, AuthorizationModule or ManagementApiModule (grep for isAdmin/Permission/role in the console path found none). (3) The HTTP user is genuinely discarded: ShellSessionCreator ignores HttpServletRequest and the shell server is constructed per-session without a subject. (4) Both shell execution paths use AUTH_DISABLED (TransactionProvidingApp:237 and Start:203), not the caller's LoginContext. (5) Consulted the enterprise enforcement points: PersonalUserManager.assertUserManager() (355-361) and EnterpriseSecurityModule:112-113 key admin rights off the transaction SecurityContext, so an AUTH_DISABLED transaction satisfies them instead of blocking. (6) dbms.shell.read_only=true (ShellSettings) would only affect the extension-built server; when dbms.shell.enabled=false (default) ShellSession falls back to `new GraphDatabaseShellServer(graph, false)` (read-write), so that setting is not a mitigation for the console path. (7) The console module can be turned off by configuration, but its default is TRUE. I did not find any source-level check that makes the console admin-only.
candidates.impact: Privilege escalation / broken authorization. A role-restricted or non-admin authenticated user obtains admin-equivalent database access: arbitrary read/write/schema operations with all role ACLs, property-permission blacklists and per-procedure admin restrictions bypassed; user and role management becomes available (dbms.security.createUser / addRoleToUser / changeUserPassword, e.g. taking over the built-in neo4j admin or minting a new admin), plus dbms.listConfig / dbms.setConfigValue / dbms.clearQueryCaches / query termination and whole-database read or wipe/dump. If the optional Groovy/BeanShell interpreters for the shell's gsh/jsh apps happen to be on the classpath, the same endpoint yields arbitrary code execution as the server process. The endpoint is reachable by default, making this a pre-authentication-free (authenticated-only) full compromise path.
candidates.prerequisites: dbms.security.auth_enabled=true (default) and dbms.security.console_module_enabled=true (default, @Internal setting whose default is TRUE) with the default SHELL engine (`unsupported.dbms.console_module.engines` default "SHELL"). Attacker must be able to reach the HTTP/HTTPS management API and possess any valid credential. For the strongest impact the instance must be Enterprise (native/role-based auth) where per-user ACLs and admin-only procedures exist; in Community every user already has FULL-style access, so the delta is mostly the user-management/config procedures. The console is reached through the same authorization filter as the rest of the server (not whitelisted), so an unauthenticated request is rejected (401).
candidates.root_cause: The management console endpoint and the shell session behind it enforce authentication but never authorization, while the shell layer deliberately creates its transactions with LoginContext.AUTH_DISABLED (SecurityContext.AUTH_DISABLED = AccessMode.Static.FULL, isAdmin() true). The user identity of the HTTP request is discarded when the shell session is created, so every shell/Cypher command runs with full privileges. Because admin-only user-management procedures (and enterprise role/property ACLs) are evaluated against the transaction's SecurityContext (ctx.get(SECURITY_CONTEXT).isAdmin()), an AUTH_DISABLED transaction satisfies them.
candidates.title: Default-enabled server console executes commands with AUTH_DISABLED, giving any authenticated user admin-equivalent privileges
candidates.trace: POST /db/manage/server/console {"engine":"shell","command":"<command>"} -> ConsoleModule mounts ConsoleService at the management API path when console_module_enabled is true -> ConsoleService.exec() (line 100-151) reads the user-supplied map, calls getSession(args) -> SessionFactoryImpl.createSession("SHELL") -> ShellSessionCreator.newSession(database, cypherExecutor, request, logProvider) constructs ShellSession, discarding the HTTP user -> ShellSession builds a SameJvmClient over the kernel GraphDatabaseShellServer (fallback server created with readOnly=false, ShellSession.java:70-85) -> ShellSession.evaluate(script) (line 88-110) forwards the command string to the shell server -> GraphDatabaseShellServer.interpretLine -> AppCommandParser resolves the leading keyword (e.g. `call`, `match`) to an app extending Start/TransactionProvidingApp -> TransactionProvidingApp.execute() begins the transaction with LoginContext.AUTH_DISABLED (line 237) and Start.exec()/createTransactionContext() does the same for Cypher (line 202-203) -> the resulting SecurityContext is AUTH_DISABLED with AccessMode.Static.FULL and isAdmin() true (SecurityContext.java:98) -> procedure invocations and ACL checks use that context (EnterpriseSecurityModule.java:112-113 passes isAdmin() into PersonalUserManager, whose assertUserManager() at line 355-361 then passes) -> the low-privileged user's command executes with full privileges.
candidates.unverified: Not runtime-verified: I could not start the server or send requests, and no test in the snapshot asserts the privilege boundary for this endpoint (the existing tests only assert 401 unauthenticated and 200 by default). Jetty/Jersey routing of the POST and the JAX-RS filter wiring were inferred from source plus the existing ITs, not executed. Whether upstream regards this as an intentional "unsupported" feature rather than a vulnerability, and whether a later fix disabled the console by default or made it use the caller's context, could not be checked (no patch/CVE data is available in this run). The conditional RCE via gsh/jsh depends on the optional Groovy/BeanShell jars being present, which I could not verify from the dependency files. Areas not inspected: the remaining ~2,000 non-Java/omitted files, packaging/config templates that could override the console default, and any plugin-based authorization rules (dbms.security.http_authorization_classes) that an operator might have configured.
candidates.weakness_type: CWE-862 Missing Authorization / CWE-269 Improper Privilege Management (privilege escalation, authorization bypass)

coverage_summary: Source scope: 9,831 root files / 9,830 model-visible files (one sensitive name/path exclusion, no symlinks, binary-like files refused/skipped). Relation index coverage is partial: 7,643 Java files parsed, 422 omitted, 3 parse errors, 106,255 symbols and 260,980 edges, with control-flow, data-flow, semantic resolution and spring DI enforcement explicitly unsupported, so every claim here is text-based and was re-verified in the source. Inspected in depth: community/server (modules: Console, Authorization/SecurityRules, Management API; rest/management/console, rest/dbms auth filters, rest/web CorsFilter, web Jetty static content, configuration ServerSettings), community/shell (ShellSession/ShellSessionCreator, GraphDatabaseShellServer, TransactionProvidingApp, cypher apps, ShellBootstrap/ShellLobby/RMI), community/security (BasicAuthManager, AuthProcedures, Credential, FileUserRepository/UserSerialization, RateLimitedAuthenticationStrategy), community/kernel security-relevant parts (FileURLAccessRule/URLAccessRules, GraphDatabaseSettings, BuiltInDbmsProcedures, ProcedureRegistry/ProcedureConfig, AccessMode/SecurityContext/AuthSubject), enterprise/security (EnterpriseSecurityModule, PersonalUserManager, UserManagementProcedures, MultiRealmAuthManager, LdapRealm), enterprise/kernel builtinprocs, enterprise/query-logging, enterprise/causal-clustering store-copy handlers (file/index requests and name matching), community/bolt (ChunkDecoder, MessageAccumulator/MessageDecoder, PackStream size handling, BasicAuthentication/BoltStateMachine auth states), cypher LOAD CSV path, community/ssl/harness/udc. Search sweeps for path traversal, command injection, XXE, deserialization, random/weak crypto, hardcoded secrets, and security-relevant regex/string handling were run repository-wide; results are reflected in the rejected leads. Not exhaustively reviewed: the remaining large modules (cypher compiler/planner, kernel storage/transaction internals, lucene/spatial indexes, causal-clustering consensus, cluster/HA, consistency-check, import tooling) and all non-Java files such as packaging/configuration templates.
limitations: No code execution, tests, or scanners were run; all conclusions are static source reading, so reachability of POST /db/manage/server/console and Jetty/Jersey filter wiring are inferred from source plus existing tests, not observed.

The relation index is partial (422 omitted files, 3 parse errors) and provides only syntactic call/containment/inheritance candidates with no data-flow or semantic resolution; index entries were used for navigation only and re-checked in source.
No patch, CVE, advisory, or fix-commit data is available in this run, so I cannot confirm whether this exact issue corresponds to the assigned case or how upstream fixed it.

Impact in Community Edition is smaller because SecurityContext.isAdmin() returns true by default there (community has no role separation); the escalation is most severe in Enterprise with role-based auth, which I could not instantiate.
The conditional RCE via the shell's gsh/jsh apps could not be verified (Groovy/BeanShell jars may not be on the distribution classpath).

Non-Java artefacts (packaging/standalone config templates, docs, any operator-provided dbms.security.http_authorization_classes security rules) were not reviewed and could change the reachable/default configuration.
I did not review the ~2,200 files outside the modules listed in the coverage summary, so other vulnerabilities may exist elsewhere in the snapshot.

rejected_leads.lead: Weak randomness for credential salts: Credential.randomSalt() uses java.util.concurrent.ThreadLocalRandom (community/kernel/src/main/java/org/neo4j/kernel/impl/security/Credential.java:156-160) instead of SecureRandom, while sibling code uses SecureRandom. Class CWE-330/338.
rejected_leads.reason: Real crypto-hygiene weakness but weak attacker control and limited impact: salts are stored next to the hashes in the auth store, so predictable salts do not materially accelerate offline cracking of the salted SHA-256 hashes, and no attacker-facing path lets an attacker choose salt inputs. No test or validation failure ties it to a concrete exploit, so it was not chosen.

rejected_leads.lead: LOAD CSV file access: FileURLAccessRule returns the requested URL unchanged when dbms.directories.import is unset (community/kernel/src/main/java/org/neo4j/kernel/impl/security/FileURLAccessRule.java:56-60), and the path check does not resolve symlinks, so file:// reads may escape the import directory.
rejected_leads.reason: Plausible information disclosure but largely documented 3.x behaviour: dbms.security.allow_csv_import_from_file_urls defaults to TRUE and the import root is optional (NO_DEFAULT), and the neighbouring tests (FileURLAccessRuleTest, LoadCsvAcceptanceTest, TransactionBoundQueryContextTest) show the escaping cases are already handled/known. Requires an authenticated user plus a permissive configuration; evidence of an unintended bypass is weaker than the console issue.

rejected_leads.lead: Shell/RMI exposure: ShellBootstrap makes an RMI ShellServer remotely available (community/shell/.../ShellBootstrap.java:43-88, RemotelyAvailableServer) and the shell runs transactions with AUTH_DISABLED, with RMI argument deserialization on the wire.
rejected_leads.reason: Not enabled by default: dbms.shell.enabled defaults to FALSE (ShellSettings.java:44), so the RMI path is opt-in; the console path reaches the same AUTH_DISABLED shell without that setting, so this was folded into the main candidate rather than reported separately.

rejected_leads.lead: Legacy HTML representation does not escape map keys (community/server/src/main/java/org/neo4j/server/rest/domain/HtmlHelper.java:115-127), so property keys containing markup could be reflected unescaped.
rejected_leads.reason: Requires a victim to request a text/html representation of data whose key an attacker controls, and the class is explicitly a legacy/throwaway renderer; no test or call path establishes a realistic XSS victim flow, so evidence is too weak.

rejected_leads.lead: Management/authorization whitelist and OPTIONS bypass in AuthorizationEnabledFilter (community/server/src/main/java/org/neo4j/server/rest/dbms/AuthorizationEnabledFilter.java:81-89; DEFAULT_URI_WHITELIST "/", "/browser.*").
rejected_leads.reason: No source-level path-confusion bypass could be demonstrated: the pattern set is small, Jetty canonicalises paths before the filter/servlet mapping, and OPTIONS is intentionally allowed for CORS preflight (CorsFilter sends no credentials). Left as unconfirmed.

rejected_leads.lead: Enterprise user-management procedures depend on injected EnterpriseUserManager built from securityContext.isAdmin() (EnterpriseSecurityModule:112-113, PersonalUserManager:355-361) so a wrong context silently grants user management.
rejected_leads.reason: Reachable only through the console/AUTH_DISABLED path already reported; treated as impact evidence for the single candidate instead of a separate finding.

summary: Neo4j 3.4.9-SNAPSHOT (community/enterprise 3.4 branch). The strongest source-evidenced issue is an authorization bypass through the default-enabled server console: the JAX-RS endpoint POST /db/manage/server/console (ConsoleService, SHELL engine) is gated only by authentication, but the shell/session it drives executes all commands in transactions created with LoginContext.AUTH_DISABLED (full access, isAdmin() true). Any authenticated user — in Enterprise, even a role-limited "reader" — therefore runs arbitrary Cypher/shell commands with admin-equivalent rights, bypassing role ACLs, property permissions and admin-only user-management procedures (create users, assign roles, change the neo4j admin password, read/write/schema everything, set config values, kill queries). RCE is additionally possible if the optional gsh/jsh script interpreters are on the classpath. No admin/role check exists anywhere on the console path, and the console module plus the SHELL engine are enabled by default; the only exposed mitigation is configuration (unsupported.dbms.console_module.enabled=false), and dbms.shell.read_only does not affect the console fallback server (created with readOnly=false). A second, much weaker lead (ThreadLocalRandom used for credential salt in Credential.randomSalt) is recorded as a rejected lead.
